en: For the first three months after their wedding, they spent happy days like an ordinary newlywed couple.
u.src: 新婚的三个月内，像一般的新婚夫妇一般，度过了幸福的时光。

en: Her husband was a man of few words, with a slightly feminine temperament.
u.src: 她的丈夫是一位不爱讲话的人，稍微有些女性气质。

en: Every day after coming home from work at the trading company, he would always spend the few hours after dinner with Nobuko.
u.src: 每天从商社下班回来之后，晚饭过后的几个小时，他一定会和信子一起度过。

en: While doing some knitting, Nobuko would talk to her husband about popular novels and plays that interested her, and now and then her conversation would also include the outlook on life of a Christian women's college.
u.src: 信子边做一些编织的手工，边对丈夫谈一些自己关注的流行小说和戏剧，偶尔谈话中还会夹杂基督信仰的女子大学的人生观。

en: After dinner, his face slightly flushed from a little drink, her husband would open the evening paper on his knees and quietly listen to Nobuko talk.
u.src: 晚饭过后，丈夫小酌过后脸色微红，打开晚报放在膝盖上，静静聆听信子的讲话。

en: But he never expressed an opinion of his own.
u.src: 但是，他从未表达做自己的意见。

en: Almost every week, her husband would take Nobuko out to Osaka Castle or to the suburbs.
u.src: 基本上每个星期，丈夫都会带着信子到大阪城里或者郊区游玩。

en: Whenever she saw people eating and drinking greedily and behaving rudely in public places such as trains and streetcars,
u.src: 每当在火车、电车等公共场合，看到那些大吃大喝举止粗鲁的人，

en: Nobuko would feel all the more that her courteous husband was refined and above the common run, and that he was her pride.
u.src: 信子就会越发觉得彬彬有礼的丈夫高雅不俗，是自己的骄傲。

en: And it was true: whether it was his hat, his suit, or his red high leather boots, her husband's clothes were always bright and immaculate, giving off a pleasant scent of soap.
u.src: 的确是这样，不管是帽子、西装，还是红色的高腰皮靴，丈夫的衣着总是光鲜亮丽，散发着好闻的香皂的香气。

en: She felt this pride even more during the summer holidays, when the couple went together to a gathering in Maiko and she compared him with his colleagues who were in the same tea room.
u.src: 这在暑假期间，他们夫妻一起去舞子参加聚会，和那些同在一个茶室的丈夫的同事们相比，信子就更加感到自豪。

en: But Nobuko had not expected that her husband seemed to be on good terms with those rough-looking colleagues.
u.src: 不过，信子没想到，丈夫和那些看起来粗鲁的同事们似乎关系很好。

en: After some time, Nobuko remembered her dream of literature, and when her husband was out, she began writing for an hour or two.
u.src: 过了一段时间，信子想到自己的文学梦，于是在丈夫外出的时候，她便开始写一两个小时的文字。

en: When her husband learned of this, he smiled and said, "My Nobuko is about to become a woman writer."
u.src: 丈夫得知这件事后，微笑的说“我的信子快要成为女作家了呀。”

en: But although she thought very hard about what to create, putting words down on paper was extremely difficult.
u.src: 但是，虽然她很努力的思考创作，但是下笔却很艰难。

ja: ぼんやりしていることに。
en: She would often notice herself resting her cheek on her hand, lost in thought as she listened to the cicadas in the pine grove.
u.src: 她经常会注意到，自己以手托腮，听着松林里的蝉鸣出神。

en: Before long, summer passed and early autumn arrived.
u.src: 很快夏天过去了，初秋来临。

en: One day, before leaving for work at the trading company, her husband wanted to change into a clean collar.
u.src: 有一天，丈夫去商社上班前，想要换干净的衣领。

en: But at the time, all the collars had been sent to the laundry.
u.src: 但当时所有的衣领都送去洗衣店了。

en: Her husband was extremely fastidious, so his face fell; as he adjusted the suspenders of his trousers, he grumbled with unusual displeasure, "If you spend all your time writing novels, I am the one who suffers."
u.src: 丈夫非常爱干净，于是耷拉下了脸，一边整理西裤的吊带，一边反常不悦的叨叨：“你只忙着写小说，那我可惨了。”

en: Nobuko had no choice but to lower her eyes and silently brush the dust from her husband's jacket.
u.src: 信子只好垂着眼睑，默不吭声的为丈夫清扫外套上的灰。

en: Two or three days later, her husband began talking about the food problem he had read about in the newspaper, and the conversation led to his saying that he hoped they could economize a little on household expenses.
u.src: 过了两三天，丈夫谈论着报纸上写的粮食问题，衍生到希望家里的家用可以节省一点。

en: "You cannot go on forever as if you were still a university girl."
u.src: “你也不能永远像个女大学生一样。”

en: Her husband even tossed out that remark.
u.src: ——丈夫还丢下了这样一句话。

en: Nobuko listened without the slightest interest, while her hands carefully embroidered an ornament onto her husband's collar.
u.src: 信子毫无兴致的听着，手里认真的给丈夫的衣领绣装饰。

en: But her husband was plainly stubborn, and he kept nagging on:
u.src: 但是丈夫显然很固执，依然不停的叨叨：

en: "Take that collar ornament in your hands, for example. It would be cheaper to buy one ready-made by someone else, would it not?"
u.src: “比如你手里的这条领饰，买别人现成做好的，更划算吧？”

en: Nobuko had nothing to say, and her husband, too, sank into a gloomy mood and listlessly looked through a business magazine.
u.src: 信子没话可说，丈夫也情绪阴沉，兴味索然的看着商业杂志。

en: But after the bedroom light had been turned off, Nobuko lay with her back to her husband and said in a low voice:
u.src: 但是，卧室关灯之后，信子背对丈夫躺着，低声说：
“我以后再也不写小说了。”
丈夫没回复。

en: After a while, Nobuko repeated what she had just said, this time in an even smaller voice.
u.src: 过了一阵，信子又说了一遍刚才这句话，声音更小了。

en: Before long, she began to cry softly.
u.src: 没多久，她开始轻轻哭泣。

en: Her husband scolded her with a few words, but her sobs still came and went.
u.src: 丈夫斥责了她几句，她的哭声依然时有时无。

en: But at some point, Nobuko had once again nestled against her husband's side...
u.src: 但是，不知道什么时候，信子又依偎在了丈夫身侧……

en: The next day, they were as affectionate as usual.
u.src: 第二天，他们像往常一样恩爱。

en: After midnight that night, her husband still had not come home from work.
u.src: 这天晚上十二点过后，丈夫依然没下班回家。

en: Nobuko waited until late at night before her husband finally staggered in reeking of alcohol, so drunk that he could not even take off his own raincoat.
u.src: 信子等到深夜，丈夫才带着一身酒气踉跄的进门，醉的自己都脱不了自己的雨衣。

en: Nobuko frowned, then efficiently took care of her husband and helped him undress.
u.src: 信子眉头蹙了起来，利落的照顾丈夫，帮他脱下衣服。

en: Even though she was so attentive, her husband still mocked her in a slurred voice: "Since I came home late tonight, you should be able to write your novel faster, shouldn't you?"
u.src: 虽然这样殷勤，但丈夫依然口齿不清的嘲讽：“今晚我晚回来，你的小说应该可以写的更快吧。”

en: He repeated such remarks over and over, like a nagging woman.
u.src: 他像个唠叨的女人一般，反反复复说着类似的话。

en: That night, Nobuko lay in bed with tears streaming down her face.
u.src: 晚上，信子躺在床上，泪流满面。

en: If Teruko saw me in such a state, she would surely cry with me.
u.src: 假如照子看到自己的这般光景，必定会和自己一起哭吧。

en: Teruko, my dear sister Teruko, you are the only one I can rely on now.
u.src: 照子，照子妹妹，我只能依靠你了。

en: In her heart, Nobuko thought again and again of her younger sister Teruko; in the bed reeking of her husband's alcohol, she tossed and turned and did not sleep all night.
u.src: 信子在心中反复思念自己的妹妹照子，在丈夫酒气熏天的床上，辗转反侧，一夜未眠。

en: But the next day, the two of them seemed as affectionate as ever again.
u.src: 但是，第二天，他们又恩爱如初似的。

en: Until late autumn, similar things happened several times.
u.src: 直到深秋，相似的事情发生了好几次。

en: Gradually, Nobuko had less and less time to write fiction, and her husband no longer showed interest in the literature she talked about.
u.src: 渐渐地，信子创作小说的时间越来越少，丈夫也对她谈论的文学不再感兴趣。

en: Every night, they sat facing the brazier and passed the time by talking about household trifles,
u.src: 每晚，他们对着火盆坐着，也就是讲讲家庭琐事来打发时间，

en: and after a little drink, her husband seemed even more interested in such topics.
u.src: 而且丈夫小酌后似乎对这些话题更感兴趣。

en: Nobuko cautiously watched her husband's expression, but he seemed not to notice,
u.src: 信子谨小慎微的观察丈夫的深色，可是丈夫似乎没有察觉，

en: biting the mustache he had recently begun to grow, and looking more cheerful than before, he said thoughtfully, "After that, how about us having a child..."
u.src: 咬着最近新留起来的胡须，比以往更加愉快，沉吟的说：“那么之后，我们生个孩子如何……”

en: At that time, Nobuko's cousin's works had begun appearing in monthly magazines.
u.src: 彼时，信子表兄的的作品开始在那段时间开始发表在每月的杂志上。

en: After Nobuko married, she no longer wrote to Shunkichi, and seemed to have forgotten that he even existed.
u.src: 信子嫁人之后，不再和俊吉写信，似乎忘记了这个人的存在。

en: What she knew about Shunkichi, such as his graduating from the literature course at university and founding a coterie magazine, all came from her younger sister's letters.
u.src: 有关俊吉的事情，诸如大学文科毕业之后，创办了同人杂志等等，都是从妹妹的来信中知道的。

en: Nor did Nobuko want to know anything about Shunkichi.
u.src: 有关俊吉的事情，信子也不想知道。

en: But when she saw her cousin's novels printed in magazines, Nobuko felt the same familiar warmth as ever.
u.src: 但是，看到表兄的小说达标在杂志上，信子觉得亲切如常。

en: As Nobuko read the novels, she often found herself smiling alone.
u.src: 信子看着小说，多次一个人不由的露出微笑。

en: In the novels, Shunkichi was, as always, much like Miyamoto Musashi, relying mainly on two modes of writing: mockery and playful wit.
u.src: 小说中，俊吉像往常一样，跟宫本武藏很像，主要使用嘲讽和戏谑两种写作方式。

en: But whether because they were psychological works or not, Nobuko felt that behind her cousin's seemingly light and witty satirical style there was something lonely, abnormal, and self-exiling.
u.src: 但是，不知道是不是心理作品，信子觉得表兄看似轻松诙谐的讽刺文风后面，好像有一种寂寞的、反常的、自我放逐的感觉。

en: At the same time, she felt guilty for having such feelings.
u.src: 与此同时，她为自己的这种感受觉得愧疚。

en: From then on, Nobuko cared for her husband even more gently and devotedly.
u.src: 从此之后，信子更加温柔贤惠的照顾丈夫。

en: Her husband noticed that his wife, seated across the long hibachi, had a gentle smile blooming on her lightly powdered face and looked younger and more beautiful than before.
u.src: 丈夫察觉到，坐在中长火盆对面的妻子，略施粉黛的脸上洋溢着温柔的笑容，看起来比以前更加年轻漂亮。

en: As she sewed, she talked about the sweet memories of their wedding in Jingdong.
u.src: 她边做针线活边谈论他们夫妻在京东举行婚礼的甜蜜往事。

en: Her husband had not expected Nobuko to remember so clearly, and he was unexpectedly pleased.
u.src: 没想到信子记得如此清晰，丈夫意料之外的开心。

en: You even remember little things like that so clearly.
u.src: “你竟然连那些小事都记得这么清楚啊。”

en: Her husband laughed and teased her, while Nobuko listened silently and answered only with a coquettish look.
u.src: 丈夫笑着调侃，信子默默听着，只回以一个媚色。

en: But as for why she could remember it so clearly, she herself could not explain.
u.src: 但是，至于自己为什么可以记得如此清楚，她也说不清楚。

en: Before long, her mother wrote to her saying that her younger sister Teruko had already completed the betrothal ceremony, and that Shunkichi had built a new house in the suburbs of Yamate and was waiting to marry Teruko.
u.src: 不久之后，母亲写信给自己，信里说妹妹照子已经完成了纳聘仪式，俊吉在山手郊外建了新房，等待迎娶照子。

en: Nobuko immediately wrote a long letter of congratulations in reply to her mother and her younger sister Teruko,
u.src: 信子马上给母亲和妹妹照子回了长长的祝福回信，

en: but when she came to the part where she wrote, "Because there is no one but me to look after the house, although I very much want to go, I regret that I truly cannot attend the wedding in person ...",
u.src: 当她写到“因为除了自己家里无人照料，尽管自己很想去，但很遗憾的确无法亲临婚礼现场……”的时候，

en: for some reason, several times she found herself unable to continue writing.
u.src: 不知何故，她数次写不下去。

en: Whenever she could not go on writing, she would always gaze into the distance at the pine grove, looking at the deep green beauty beneath the early winter sky.
u.src: 写不下去的时候，她必定会远眺松林，看着初冬的天空下，郁郁苍苍的美景。

en: That night, Nobuko told her husband about her younger sister Teruko's marriage plans,
u.src: 当天夜里，信子对丈夫说起妹妹照子的婚事，

en: and her husband smiled as he always did, listening with considerable interest as she imitated the way Teruko spoke.
u.src: 丈夫像以往一样微笑，颇有兴致的听她模仿照子讲话的语调。

en: But Nobuko felt as though she were telling herself about Teruko's marriage.
u.src: 但是，信子却觉得她是在对自己讲述照子结婚的事情。

en: "All right, let's go to bed early."
u.src: “好了，早点睡觉吧。”

en: Two or three hours later, her husband rose from beside the brazier, stroking his beard as he went.
u.src: ——两三个小时候之后，丈夫一边摸着胡子一边起身离开火盆。

en: Nobuko did not know what wedding gift she ought to give Teruko,
u.src: 信子不知道送什么贺礼给照子好，

en: and, out of boredom, she wrote in the charcoal ash with the fire tongs,
u.src: 她无聊的用火筷子在炭灰上写字，

en: then suddenly looked up and said to her husband, "It feels a little strange to think that I will have a brother-in-law too."
u.src: 她抬头突然对丈夫说：“想到我也有妹夫了，总有些奇怪。”

en: "What is strange about that? You have a younger sister, after all."
u.src: “这有什么奇怪的，你有妹妹啊。”

en: Although her husband said this, Nobuko still fell silent, as if lost in thought.
u.src: 虽然丈夫如是说，但信子还是若有所思般沉默。

en: One day in mid-December, Teruko and Shunkichi held their wedding.
u.src: 十二月中旬的一天，照子和俊吉举行了婚礼。

en: That day, before noon had come, snow began to fall.
u.src: 那天，未到中午，就飘起来雪花。

en: After eating lunch alone, Nobuko still felt as though the taste of fish lingered in her mouth.
u.src: 信子一个人吃完午饭，总觉得鱼的味道一直留在口中。

en: I wonder whether it is snowing in Tokyo too.
u.src: “不知道东京是不是也下雪了呢？”

en: Lost in thought, she lay on her back beside the long brazier in the sitting room, without moving.
u.src: 她若有所思的仰躺在起居室的长火盆旁一动不动。

en: The snow fell harder and harder, but the fishy smell in her mouth was still there...
u.src: 雪越来越大，但是口中的鱼腥味却一直还在……
